summary: Council formally endorsed Steinbach Community Outreach and Eden Health Care Services' new supportive housing project, The Bridge on Third, with a letter the groups can attach to grant applications. Members praised the first Bridge (funded by the province in 2022 with the city choosing the operator). No city money or land was offered.
status_detail: Endorsement resolution R26-096 passed; support is a letter only.
reasons: other-governments-fund: Model: senior government funds, city picks the organization (Michael Zwaagstra)

title: 2-storey cap from 2013 lifted for apartments on Lund Road
summary: Land at 80/81 Lund Road was zoned medium density in 2013 with a voluntary 2-storey limit to win neighbour support. Council allowed a third storey (no change in unit count, per the applicant) despite neighbours' traffic concerns.
status_detail: Variance V-2026-13 approved subject to a development agreement (R26-132).
figures: Conceptually ~240 units on the sites (applicant rep, Jul 7, 2026 0:21:55); 45-ft buffer to homes to the south (Warkentin 0:06:39)
public: L.S. and J.W. (Westview area) raised traffic, children's safety and drainage.

title: Maplewood Manor 19-bed assisted-living expansion approved
summary: Maplewood Manor got conditional use to consolidate seven Hospital Street lots and add a 19-bed assisted-living building. Members said seniors are being placed in care far from Steinbach.
status_detail: CU-2026-07 approved subject to a development agreement (R26-133).
figures: 19 beds; 7 houses removed (Warkentin and applicant, Jul 7, 2026 0:32:29, 0:34:05)
public: No objections.

title: Williams Creek Phase 1: 153 lots off Loewen Blvd
summary: A 74-acre area zoned residential in 2012–13 but never built was reconfigured for 153 lots (single-unit, low and medium density) with six new roads and a concrete-bottom drainage swale. Neighbours asked that lots stay single-family and raised drainage and parking. Council approved second reading and the subdivision unanimously, declining to add rules beyond the zoning by-law.
status_detail: By-law 2283 second reading (R26-156) and subdivision 4451-2025-9083 (R26-157) approved Aug 4, 2026; third reading awaits the development agreement (not given by Oct 20, 2026).
figures: 153 lots in phase 1 (Warkentin, Aug 4, 2026 0:05:59); ~74 acres, ~155 potential lots (Siemens, Jul 7, 2026 0:49:12)
reasons: market-decides: Mix of single-family and medium density is market-driven; developer decides (Jake Hiebert); fairness-precedent: Won't add ad hoc rules beyond the zoning by-law on a long-planned project (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: S.B. and G.W. asked to keep lots 16–41 single-family rather than duplexes and raised drainage and parking. The applicant (M.J.) said duplex lots are what many buyers can afford.
mover: Susan Penner (1st); Michael Zwaagstra (2nd); Damian Penner (subdivision)
seconder: Jac Siemens (1st); Jake Hiebert (2nd); Bill Hiebert (subdivision)
notes: J. Hiebert's Aug 4 remarks sit on a merged label (Jake/Bill Hiebert, medium) and are paraphrased, not quoted; the mayor named "Councilor Hebert" as seconder.

title: Six-storey, 81-suite 55+ building at Bridgepark approved 6-1
summary: Bridgepark Manor asked to build 6 storeys (81 suites for 55+) on land already zoned medium density beside its existing buildings, with reduced parking. Many Georgetown and Albert Street residents objected, citing sewer backups, flooding, height and privacy. Council approved 6 storeys with 1.25 stalls per unit 6-1; Siemens wanted 6-storey buildings kept to the CBD.
status_detail: Variance V-2026-14 approved (R26-147) after Siemens's motion to deny found no seconder.
figures: 81 suites (applicant rep, Jul 21, 2026 0:26:41); 1.25 stalls/unit (R26-147); about 220 people on the waiting list (S. Penner 0:59:04)
reasons: neighbourhood-not-ready: 6-storey buildings belong in the CBD; area is all 3-storey (Jac Siemens); infrastructure-capacity: Sewer and drainage already overloaded (residents, not council) (residents)
public: M.R., G.R., B.K., G.K., E.K., A.A. and D.J. objected (sewer backups, flooding, height, privacy, traffic); D.J. said he did not oppose 55+ housing but questioned infrastructure. The Bridgepark representative (N.T.) said on-site stormwater rules hold runoff to pre-development rates.
notes: The Jul 21, 2026 recording starts partway through the public hearing, so staff's introduction is missing. The speaker map labels S. Penner's voice 'Susan Penner (council-meeting...)'; confidence as mapped.

title: 12-unit building at 58 Giesbrecht St approved over neighbour objections
summary: A double lot at 58 Giesbrecht St was rezoned for a 2-storey, 12-unit building next to land already zoned medium density. Neighbours objected (privacy, drainage, trees, "end of life" claims about the house) and asked whether the city has a plan other than infill. Council approved unanimously.
status_detail: By-law 2285 second reading Sep 1, 2026 (R26-179); third reading carried Oct 20, 2026 (transcript; minutes not yet available).
figures: 12 units, 2 storeys (Warkentin, Sep 1, 2026 0:06:25)
public: K.V., T.N., H.K. and G.W. objected; T.N. asked whether the city has a plan for where density goes instead of lot-by-lot infill.
resolution_no: R26-166 (1st), R26-179 (2nd), 3rd Oct 20, 2026 (not yet in minutes)
seconder: Susan Penner (1st); Bill Hiebert (2nd); "Councillor Pinner" (3rd, transcript)

title: 12 units at 288 Henry St approved 6-1 over J. Hiebert's parking concerns
summary: Next to the 6-plex approved at 286 Henry in 2025, an applicant sought medium-density zoning and a narrower site width for a 3-storey, 12-unit building near the hospital. One neighbour raised sightlines and trees. Council approved 6-1; J. Hiebert objected at every reading over visitor parking and emergency vehicles on a narrow street.
status_detail: By-law 2286 second reading (R26-200) and Variance V-2026-16 (R26-201) Oct 6, 2026; third reading carried Oct 20, 2026 (transcript; J. Hiebert restated his objection).
figures: 12 units, 3 storeys, 20 stalls required and provided (Zwaagstra, Oct 6, 2026 1:15:18); site width 65 ft vs 75 ft (Warkentin 1:02:44)
reasons: parking-rules: No visitor parking on Henry St near the hospital; street used by emergency vehicles (Jake Hiebert)
public: A neighbour raised sightlines and tree loss, and the applicant adjusted the plan; another resident questioned tree replacement beside a parking lot.

title: 20 townhouse-style units at 330 McKenzie denied, against staff advice
summary: An applicant proposed rezoning a 100 x 300 ft lot on arterial McKenzie Ave for a 2-storey, 20-unit townhouse-style building with no variances; staff recommended approval. About 60 letters and many speakers objected. Council unanimously denied it, saying this stretch, half a mile from Main Street and still single-family in character, is not a transition area yet, unlike 492–506 McKenzie approved months earlier.
status_detail: By-law 2281 denied at second reading Oct 6, 2026 (R26-199).
figures: 20 units (applicant, Oct 6, 2026 0:08:17; staff report said 24 suites, 0:06:00); 34 letters in package + 28 more at the meeting (Warkentin 0:06:00); 7 existing RMD sites on McKenzie between Main and Brandt (Warkentin)
reasons: neighbourhood-not-ready: Not a transitional zone; infill policy does not apply; does not fit neighbourhood character (Jake Hiebert); neighbours-object: Council must listen to ~60 objectors (Jake Hiebert); neighbourhood-not-ready: Character still single-family; would trigger rapid transition of the area (Damian Penner); neighbourhood-not-ready: 'This is maybe not the time' (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: A.N., K.B. and many neighbours objected (precedent, trees, privacy, traffic, cycling safety, reliance on the zoning plan). K.U., a realtor, said the precedent was already set by the earlier McKenzie approval and that the 2-storey plan was modest.
notes: No speaker map for Oct 6, 2026; councillor identities are from chair cues and the minutes (see id_evidence). Residents A.N. and K.B. self-identified at the podium.

title: Mayor's task force on keeping aging seniors in Steinbach
summary: Council created the "Rooted in Community" task force to find practical ways for seniors awaiting personal-care-home placement to stay in Steinbach, after S. Penner and the mayor raised it with the health minister. The mayor said the aim is low-cost solutions, not more care-home beds.
status_detail: Terms of reference approved and four members appointed (R26-205); no report yet.
figures: "PCHs at $1 million a bed" (mayor, Oct 6, 2026 1:45:28)
reasons: other-governments-fund: Care homes are provincial; city seeks cost-saving ideas the province would adopt (Mayor Earl Funk)
